nodes.label: Mechanism-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: Causal compression converts historically expensive causal sequences into maintained transitions that are cheap to invoke under a declared continuation contract.
falsifiers: A bounded transition whose invocation burden does not decline relative to construction burden after reuse and maintenance are introduced.

nodes.label: Compression-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: Representational causal compression preserves continuation-relevant distinctions in a future-sufficient present state, while structural causal compression embodies historical work in maintained infrastructure that makes a transition cheaply available.
falsifiers: A case in which the proposed distinction cannot separate internal state abstraction from maintained transition infrastructure under the declared contract.

nodes.label: Gap-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: The invocation-construction gap is an observable asymmetry between the work required to establish reliable transition capability and the work required for local invocation.
falsifiers: A specified transition for which construction and invocation workloads remain comparable after contract, maintenance, and reuse are controlled.

nodes.label: Lifecycle-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: Causal compression participates in a lifecycle in which cheap invocation expands reachable states, selection creates commitments, maintenance preserves compiled structure, and re-evaluation determines renewal, replacement, or retirement.
falsifiers: A bounded system in which durable compressed capability persists while every lifecycle stage is absent or persistently unable to perform its declared function.

nodes.label: Headroom-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: Increasing nominal capability does not necessarily increase adaptive headroom; commitment burden and maintenance drift can narrow effective reachable futures while raw capability grows.
falsifiers: A controlled workload in which the proposed burden/reachability coupling is absent under declared constraints.

nodes.label: QueueMigration-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: Increasing candidate-generation capacity should move observed bottlenecks downstream when evaluation, integration, maintenance, or retirement capacity does not scale with generation.
falsifiers: A controlled capacity-scaling experiment in which downstream service remains non-bottlenecked without additional evaluation, integration, maintenance, or retirement capacity.

nodes.label: Timescale-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: Under environmental change, an intermediate structural-update regime can outperform both excessively rapid updating and excessively slow updating on a predeclared adaptive-performance measure.
falsifiers: A repeated-seed dynamical benchmark in which performance is monotone across the declared update-rate range or the result disappears under matched controls.

nodes.label: Magic-001
nodes.scope: Paper-level proposition
nodes.claim_text: The phenomenology of magic is associated with a large construction-invocation gap, reliable and consequential transition behavior, and causal depth hidden from the local invocation loop.
falsifiers: A comparative protocol showing no relationship between the declared gap/reliability/consequence variables and reports of magical appearance.

nodes.label: CausalCompression
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.summary: A transformation that reduces runtime decision burden by compiling continuation-relevant consequences of history into present structure under a declared contract.

nodes.label: InformationalPersistence
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.summary: A lesson surviving in a state representation after the originating episode leaves active control.

nodes.label: AttentionalPersistence
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.summary: The originating episode remaining in the active control loop of a later decision.

nodes.label: StructuralUpdateRate
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.summary: The rate at which evaluated experience is allowed to modify learned structural state.

nodes.label: AdaptiveHeadroom
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.summary: Gross capacity to change minus capacity encumbered by current commitments.

nodes.label: ContractRelativeReachability
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.summary: The set of future states reachable within declared time, cost, risk, and commitment bounds.

nodes.label: causal_compression_definition
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Causal compression is contract-relative: it preserves distinctions required by future decisions while discarding historical detail that no longer changes the continuation problem.

nodes.label: episode_retirement_definition
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Episode retirement does not imply zero learning; it means the episode leaves active control after its decision-relevant information has passed through evaluation and update.

nodes.label: informational_attentional_distinction
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Informational persistence and attentional persistence are distinct observables; adaptive systems may benefit from the first while suppressing the second.

nodes.label: expertise_as_compiled_history
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Expertise can be modeled as history compiled into present action structure with lower runtime burden than replaying the originating history.

nodes.label: update_rate_tradeoff
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: An update rate that is too high can produce policy thrashing from noisy outcomes, while an update rate that is too low can preserve obsolete structure under environmental change.

nodes.label: presence_as_compression
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Presence is a contract-relative condition in which continuation-relevant history is available in present state without requiring the historical payload to remain in active attention.

nodes.label: lifecycle_requirement
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Durable capability requires coupled generation, evaluation, selection, compilation, maintenance, re-evaluation, and renewal, replacement, or retirement.

nodes.label: headroom_accounting
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Adaptive headroom is a first-order approximation given by gross change-support capacity minus capacity encumbered by existing commitments; raw capability count is not the same quantity.

nodes.label: capability_headroom_nonimplication
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: An increase in possessed capabilities does not by itself imply an increase in gross adaptive capacity or uncommitted adaptive headroom.

nodes.label: safe_structural_forgetting
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: Retirement releases option value only when it preserves the required continuation contract and releases more future capacity than it destroys through transition and capability loss.

nodes.label: magic_evidence_boundary
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: A low-cost local invocation can reflect historically expensive compiled causal work, but apparent magic is not evidence of reliability, causal understanding, or supernatural mechanism.

nodes.label: validation_program
nodes.scope: AxiomReason descriptive Lean package
nodes.claim_text: The framework is an open measurement program: bounded instruments should compare runtime burden, update behavior, maintenance burden, transition cost, reachability, and falsifiers without treating synthetic fixtures as universal laws.
